rule_summary: Full-time foster care in another family (Vollzeitpflege) can be for a set time or long term. Special forms of family care should exist for children with high needs.
Anyone who takes a child into their home day and night needs a foster care permit (Pflegeerlaubnis). There are exceptions, listed in the same section.
notes: No permit is needed when the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) places the child as help with upbringing. City pages say the office still checks suitability by the same criteria.

rule_summary: Relatives up to the third degree, by blood or marriage, need no foster care permit. Nor does anyone caring for a child for up to 8 weeks.
The permit must be refused if the child's welfare is not secure in the foster home. The youth welfare office should check on site, as each case needs.
notes: The law sets no fixed term for the permit. The office must withdraw it if the child is at risk and the carer cannot remove the risk.

rule_summary: Youth welfare offices must not place children with people convicted of listed sexual or violent offences. They should ask for an enhanced police certificate (erweitertes Führungszeugnis) at the start and at regular intervals.
legal_citation: SGB VIII § 72a(1); applied to the permit by § 44(2)

rule_summary: An enhanced police certificate is issued for work that involves supervising or caring for children. The person applying must bring a written request from the body that needs it.
notes: The receiving body may use the data only to check suitability, and must delete it at the latest 6 months after the activity ends.

rule_summary: The foster care permit is granted by the youth welfare office for the area where the foster carer usually lives.
notes: So people apply to their own office by home address. When a child is placed from another area, the office where the carer lives should be involved (§ 37c(3)).

rule_summary: Foster carers have a right to advice and support before a child moves in and for as long as the child stays. Groups of foster carers should be advised, supported and funded.
A foster child's help plan records the agreed support for the carer and the amount of the monthly payment.
The youth welfare office must cover the child's upkeep. It pays a monthly lump sum for material costs and for care and upbringing.
notes: A carer who is a direct relative and can afford it may get a reduced amount for material costs.

rule_summary: Each Land sets the monthly lump sums under its own law, graded by the child's age.
notes: If the child lives in another office's area, the rates of the place where the foster home is should apply (§ 39(4)).

rule_summary: The monthly payment also covers proven accident insurance costs and half of proven costs for a suitable pension for the carer.
If the carer receives child benefit for the foster child, half the first-child amount is deducted from the payment. For a child who is not the eldest, a quarter is deducted.
One-off grants can be paid, for example to equip the foster home, for important personal events and for the child's holidays.
A single adopter must be at least 25. In a married couple adopting together, one must be at least 25 and the other at least 21.
notes: A person adopting their spouse's child must be at least 21.

rule_summary: A person who is not married can adopt a child only alone. A married couple can adopt only together.
notes: So unmarried couples cannot adopt an unrelated child together. The 2022 BAGLJÄ guidance covers applications from married same-sex couples.

rule_summary: An unmarried partner can adopt their partner's child if the couple share a stable household. That usually means 4 years together, or a shared child.
A court should normally grant an adoption only after the child has lived with the adopter for a suitable time (Adoptionspflege).
Adoption is allowed when it serves the child's welfare and a parent-child bond can be expected.

Only youth welfare offices, Land youth offices and approved non-profit agencies may place children for adoption. Approved agencies include those of Diakonie, Caritas and the Workers' Welfare Association (AWO).
notes: A non-profit agency needs approval from the central adoption office of the Land youth office.

rule_summary: On request, the adoption office checks the applicants' general suitability. The check covers family life, health, social setting, motives and which children they could care for.
notes: The office writes a report and tells applicants the result. A positive report must not be handed to them.

rule_summary: For people who want to adopt, the adoption office of the area where they usually live is responsible.
A child may move in with applicants for adoptive care only once their suitability is established.
Applicants have a right to support from the adoption office before and during placement and after the adoption order. Support covers advice, information on the process and openness with the child.
notes: Rights to support after adoption came in with the Adoption Help Act (Adoptionshilfe-Gesetz) in force from 1 April 2021.

rule_summary: Before a step-parent adoption, the parents, the adopter and the child must get advice from an adoption office. The office issues a certificate.
notes: This does not apply if the adopter was married to the parent when the child was born.

rule_summary: An international adoption must go through a central adoption office or an approved agency for international adoption. An adoption abroad without one is banned.
notes: Local youth welfare offices no longer place children from abroad (federal family ministry leaflet, March 2021).

rule_summary: The Adoption Help Act took effect on 1 April 2021. It added support after adoption, more openness, and the ban on unaccompanied adoptions from abroad.
notes: Leaflet from the federal family ministry, March 2021. The link now redirects to the renamed ministry site.

rule_summary: The German Association for Public and Private Welfare (Deutscher Verein) recommends 1,203 euro a month for ages 0 to 6 in 2026. That is 764 euro for material costs plus 439 euro for care and upbringing.
notes: Ages 6 to 12: 923 + 439 = 1,362 euro. Ages 12 to 18: 1,072 + 439 = 1,511 euro. Recommendation DV 7/25 of 16 September 2025. It is not binding; each Land decides.

rule_summary: The Deutscher Verein recommends 439 euro a month for care and upbringing in 2026, the same for every age.
notes: The 2025 amount was 430 euro.

rule_summary: For 2026 the Deutscher Verein recommends refunding half of proven pension costs for each foster child, at least 56 euro a month.
notes: It also recommends refunding proven accident insurance costs of up to 199.67 euro a year for each caring parent.

rule_summary: There are no fixed age limits. The federal family portal says foster parents should usually be at least 25.
Foster care services make sure the age gap suits a family. The portal says carers should usually be no older than 63 when the child turns 18.
Fostering is open to people of any family status: couples with or without children, opposite-sex or same-sex couples, and single people.
Applicants usually need to show orderly finances and enough living space.
notes: No income figure is given.

rule_summary: Working is not in itself a bar to fostering. Foster parents have the same right to parental leave (Elternzeit) as other parents.
notes: The portal advises planning enough time at the start.

rule_summary: No teaching or care qualification is needed to foster.
Every adult in the household must apply for an enhanced police certificate and give it to the youth welfare office.
notes: Checklist dated 3 November 2026 in the file name.

rule_summary: Applicants bring a doctor's certificate that they can care for a child in the long term. An illness is not an automatic bar.
The suitability check includes personal talks and home visits. They cover motives, life story, views on upbringing and attitude to the child's birth family.
Applicants show proof of income and a tenancy agreement or proof of ownership, for safe space that suits the child's age.
notes: The checklist does not say renting is a bar.

rule_summary: Applicants attend an information evening and preparation training. Training covers attachment, stress, the birth family, contact visits, life-story work, law and daily support.
notes: Length and format vary between youth welfare offices.

rule_summary: Foster carers should be willing to keep learning. Many services offer further training, carer groups and supervision.
The law sets no upper age. Guidance says adopters' age should fit a natural parent-child age gap, judged case by case.
notes: Recommendations of the Federal Working Group of Land Youth Offices (BAGLJÄ), 9th edition 2022. They are guidance, not law.

rule_summary: Adopters must be able to care for the child for many years. They may be asked for an official medical or psychological check, and they pay for it.
notes: Recommendations of the Federal Working Group of Land Youth Offices (BAGLJÄ), 9th edition 2022. They are guidance, not law.

rule_summary: Applicants must show that the child's upbringing is financially secure. Adoption is possible only in exceptional cases for people on state benefits or in personal insolvency.
notes: Recommendations of the Federal Working Group of Land Youth Offices (BAGLJÄ), 9th edition 2022. They are guidance, not law.

rule_summary: In the first year after placement, one or both parents should give the child intensive care. Later, one parent should be the main carer.
notes: Recommendations of the Federal Working Group of Land Youth Offices (BAGLJÄ), 9th edition 2022. They are guidance, not law. Applicants who will not adapt their work to the child do not meet the requirements.

rule_summary: Applicants give the adoption office an enhanced police certificate. Convictions for sexual or violent offences listed in SGB VIII § 72a rule a person out.
notes: Recommendations of the Federal Working Group of Land Youth Offices (BAGLJÄ), 9th edition 2022. They are guidance, not law. The family court can ask for the full criminal record.

rule_summary: The suitability check needs detailed talks, home visits and preparation seminars on adoption.
notes: Recommendations of the Federal Working Group of Land Youth Offices (BAGLJÄ), 9th edition 2022. They are guidance, not law.

rule_summary: Preparation seminars should cover motives, the applicants' own life story, law, open adoption, the child's origins and attachment.
notes: Recommendations of the Federal Working Group of Land Youth Offices (BAGLJÄ), 9th edition 2022. They are guidance, not law. Seminars are part of the suitability check.

rule_summary: Adoption by a single person needs a very careful check. Guidance names cases where it fits, such as an existing close bond with the child.
notes: Recommendations of the Federal Working Group of Land Youth Offices (BAGLJÄ), 9th edition 2022. They are guidance, not law. Single applicants should have a stable support network.

rule_summary: The adoptive care period before the court order should usually be at least 1 year.
notes: Recommendations of the Federal Working Group of Land Youth Offices (BAGLJÄ), 9th edition 2022. They are guidance, not law.

rule_summary: There should be enough living space for the child to have a place to retreat and grow, suited to their age.
notes: Recommendations of the Federal Working Group of Land Youth Offices (BAGLJÄ), 9th edition 2022. They are guidance, not law.

rule_summary: Baden-Baden pays 1,203 euro a month for ages 0 to 6 from 1 January 2026. Its rates follow the joint recommendations of the KVJS, the district and city associations.
notes: Ages 6 to 12: 1,362 euro. Ages 12 to 18: 1,511 euro. Each youth welfare office sets its own rates; Baden-Baden's guideline dated 1 January 2026 is one example.

rule_summary: Baden-Baden refunds half of proven pension costs for each foster child, at least 56 euro a month in 2026.
Karlsruhe says the age gap between carer and child in full-time foster care should usually be no more than 45 years.
notes: Seen in a search summary of Karlsruhe pages. City practice, not a Land rule.

rule_summary: Since January 2025 Karlsruhe pays foster parents a payment like parental allowance for the first 12 months after a child moves in.
notes: City news item seen in search results. Foster parents get no federal parental allowance (Elterngeld).

rule_summary: Ludwigsburg district asks adoption applicants to be married and to have lived together for some time. It also looks for a natural age gap to a baby.
notes: District practice. Federal law lets single people adopt alone (BGB § 1741).

rule_summary: Bavaria's city and district associations raised the recommended amount for care and upbringing from 350 to 430 euro a month from 1 January 2026.
notes: Letter of 25 June 2025. Bavaria keeps its own recommendations rather than the Deutscher Verein's. Upkeep follows the federal minimum child support rules.

rule_summary: Nuremberg's page lists 1,143 euro a month up to age 6, with 350 euro of it for upbringing.
notes: Ages 7 to 12: 1,287 euro; from 13: 1,477 euro. The page still shows 350 euro for upbringing, so it may predate the 2026 rise.

rule_summary: People who want to foster contact the youth welfare office of the Berlin district where they live.
For a long-term placement, the age gap between carer and child should not be more than 45 years.
Placements should usually be arranged so that they end by the time the carer turns 63.
notes: Berlin administrative rules for foster care (AV-Pflege), in force since 1 July 2004 and linked from the current Senate page.

rule_summary: Carers must not depend on the money meant for the child to cover their own living costs.
notes: Berlin administrative rules for foster care (AV-Pflege), in force since 1 July 2004 and linked from the current Senate page. The Senate page says the same.

rule_summary: A foster family should care for no more than 3 foster children. Exceptions are allowed, for example to keep siblings together.
notes: Berlin administrative rules for foster care (AV-Pflege), in force since 1 July 2004 and linked from the current Senate page.

rule_summary: A carer taking a foster child for the first time must complete foster parent training (Pflegeelternschulung).
notes: Berlin administrative rules for foster care (AV-Pflege), in force since 1 July 2004 and linked from the current Senate page. Familien für Kinder runs an information evening and a one-day seminar; both partners attend.

rule_summary: Carers must commit to regular further training and advice, as agreed in the child's help plan.
notes: Berlin administrative rules for foster care (AV-Pflege), in force since 1 July 2004 and linked from the current Senate page.

rule_summary: Part-time work is possible. The amount of paid work is agreed in the child's help plan.
notes: Berlin administrative rules for foster care (AV-Pflege), in force since 1 July 2004 and linked from the current Senate page.

rule_summary: A placement needs a certificate of health for the carer and other household members, and a current police certificate.
notes: Berlin administrative rules for foster care (AV-Pflege), in force since 1 July 2004 and linked from the current Senate page.

rule_summary: Since 1 January 2025 foster families can claim a start bonus (Startbonus Pflegekind) of 924 euro a month, on top of the usual payments.
notes: A pilot scheme. Search results say it continues in 2026 and 2027. Claims go to Familien für Kinder gGmbH.

rule_summary: Familien für Kinder says about 9 months pass from the first information evening to a foster child moving in.
notes: The same page says adopting a child takes 2 to 7 years.

rule_summary: One adoption office at the Senate Department handles adoption placement for all 12 Berlin district youth welfare offices.
The central adoption office for Berlin and Brandenburg charges a flat fee of 1,200 euro for its part in an international adoption.
notes: Seen in a search summary of the ministry pages, citing its fee rules.

rule_summary: Potsdam says foster parents should be physically and mentally healthy and resilient, and able to reflect on their role and keep learning.
Bremen raised foster payments from 1 January 2026 in line with the Deutscher Verein. Material costs are 764 euro a month for ages 0 to 6.
notes: Seen in search results; the document refused our reader (403). The amount for care and upbringing was not shown.

rule_summary: Couples with or without children and single people with a stable social network can become foster parents.
notes: Bremen service portal, seen in search results; the page refused our reader (403).

rule_summary: Applicants must first qualify by taking courses, and then apply. PiB – Pflegekinder in Bremen checks their suitability.
notes: The portal says people can also apply online with a form called Pflegeeltern werden.

rule_summary: Hamburg pays 1,397 euro a month for ages 0 to 5 from 1 January 2026. This includes 194 euro for extras such as trips and celebrations.
notes: Ages 6 to 11: 1,556 euro. From 12: 1,705 euro. A 77 euro bonus is added for a new placement of a child aged 14 or over. Set on 30 September 2025.

rule_summary: In a couple, one partner should be at least 25 and the other at least 21.
notes: Hamburg instruction for the foster care service (Fachanweisung Pflegekinderdienst), in force 1 April 2019. It says its term ended 31 December 2023; we found no newer version.

rule_summary: The age gap between carer and foster child should not be more than 50 years. Exceptions are possible.
notes: Hamburg instruction for the foster care service (Fachanweisung Pflegekinderdienst), in force 1 April 2019. It says its term ended 31 December 2023; we found no newer version.

rule_summary: Anyone with an entry listed in SGB VIII § 72a on their enhanced police certificate cannot foster. This applies to every household member aged 18 or over.
notes: Hamburg instruction for the foster care service (Fachanweisung Pflegekinderdienst), in force 1 April 2019. It says its term ended 31 December 2023; we found no newer version.

rule_summary: The foster care service asks for a new enhanced police certificate from every household member aged 18 or over every 3 years.
notes: Hamburg instruction for the foster care service (Fachanweisung Pflegekinderdienst), in force 1 April 2019. It says its term ended 31 December 2023; we found no newer version.

rule_summary: Applicants need a certificate from the public health office and a drug test. Signs of addiction or serious illness can rule a person out.
notes: Hamburg instruction for the foster care service (Fachanweisung Pflegekinderdienst), in force 1 April 2019. It says its term ended 31 December 2023; we found no newer version. Household members aged 18 or over are checked too, with some exceptions.

rule_summary: A person who needs the foster payment to support their family cannot foster. Proof of income and a credit report are required.
notes: Hamburg instruction for the foster care service (Fachanweisung Pflegekinderdienst), in force 1 April 2019. It says its term ended 31 December 2023; we found no newer version.

rule_summary: The child needs their own bed and enough space. Housing is too small if 2 people have under 35 square metres, plus 10 for each extra person.
notes: Hamburg instruction for the foster care service (Fachanweisung Pflegekinderdienst), in force 1 April 2019. It says its term ended 31 December 2023; we found no newer version.

rule_summary: The rooms the child uses every day should be kept smoke-free.
notes: Hamburg instruction for the foster care service (Fachanweisung Pflegekinderdienst), in force 1 April 2019. It says its term ended 31 December 2023; we found no newer version.

rule_summary: Dangerous items such as weapons and medicines must be out of the child's reach.
notes: Hamburg instruction for the foster care service (Fachanweisung Pflegekinderdienst), in force 1 April 2019. It says its term ended 31 December 2023; we found no newer version.

rule_summary: People who keep dangerous pets, or so many pets that hygiene suffers, cannot foster.
notes: Hamburg instruction for the foster care service (Fachanweisung Pflegekinderdienst), in force 1 April 2019. It says its term ended 31 December 2023; we found no newer version.

rule_summary: Applicants must show they attended the information evenings and the basic training (Grundqualifizierung).
notes: Hamburg instruction for the foster care service (Fachanweisung Pflegekinderdienst), in force 1 April 2019. It says its term ended 31 December 2023; we found no newer version.

rule_summary: No child is placed during a pregnancy, while the youngest child is under 2, or within 2 years of a previous placement.
notes: Hamburg instruction for the foster care service (Fachanweisung Pflegekinderdienst), in force 1 April 2019. It says its term ended 31 December 2023; we found no newer version. Siblings placed together are an exception.

rule_summary: Wiesbaden says couples with or without children and single people with a stable social network can foster.
notes: Seen in a search summary. City practice, not a Land rule.

rule_summary: International adoption for people living in Hesse goes through the joint central adoption office of Rhineland-Palatinate and Hesse in Mainz, or an approved agency.
Schwerin's preparation course for foster parents lasts 40 hours. The non-profit Pro Kind runs it.
notes: From a search summary of Schwerin pages; a course was due to start on 12 March 2026. City practice.

rule_summary: Schwerin says the application phase takes up to half a year.
Rostock foster parents must take part in at least 2 training events a year.
notes: From a search summary of the Rostock events calendar for March 2024 to March 2025. City practice.

rule_summary: No foster payment is made during adoptive care, because the applicants take on the parents' rights and duties.
notes: Lower Saxony service portal, seen in search results.

rule_summary: After adoptive care of usually at least 1 year, applicants file a notarised request with the family court. The court takes at least 3 months.
notes: Lower Saxony service portal, seen in search results.

rule_summary: The Hannover Region adoption office runs information events about 4 times a year. People can apply only after attending one.
notes: 4 is the number of events a year, not a requirement to attend 4. The application forms are handed out at the event.

rule_summary: From 1 January 2026, North Rhine-Westphalia pays 1,203 euro a month up to age 6. That is 764 euro for material costs and 439 euro for upbringing.
legal_citation: Runderlass Pauschalbeträge bei Vollzeitpflege, 23rd amendment of 29 January 2026 (MB.NRW 2026 Nr. 61)
notes: Ages 6 to 12: 1,362 euro. Ages 12 to 18, and young adults in some cases: 1,511 euro. The same amounts as the Deutscher Verein.

rule_summary: In Cologne, applicants attend 4 seminar days run by the German Red Cross, usually spread over 6 months. The city pays.
notes: City practice.

rule_summary: Cologne charges no fees. Applicants pay any cost of the doctor's certificate. The city gives a letter so the police certificate is free.
Düsseldorf's preparation seminar runs over 6 evenings of about 3 hours each, followed by a talk and a home visit.
notes: 18 hours is our total of 6 evenings of 3 hours. The city web page says 5 dates, twice a year.

rule_summary: Düsseldorf says to allow 6 to 9 months for the preparation process.
notes: 9 is the upper end of the range.

rule_summary: Düsseldorf says a foster child should have their own room in the long term. Young children may share at first.
Düsseldorf pays a special payment like parental allowance when its service places a child long term with a family living in the city.
notes: Foster parents can take parental leave but get no federal parental allowance.

rule_summary: In Essen, several talks with a worker are followed by 2 weekend seminars. Preparation takes about 6 months.
notes: The 6 months figure is from a search summary of Essen pages.

rule_summary: In Mainz, the youth welfare office checks suitability first. A compulsory preparation course follows before a child is placed.
notes: City practice.

rule_summary: Mainz says the monthly foster payment is graded by age and set by the Land youth office.
notes: We could not reach the Land's 2026 amounts.

rule_summary: Mainz says foster parents can be married, unmarried or single, with or without children of their own.
In the Saarbrücken Regional Association, adoption applicants must attend a weekend seminar run by the youth welfare office.
notes: Local practice. A home visit is also part of the process.

rule_summary: Saarbrücken expects one parent to cut back paid work for a time after the child arrives, using parental leave.
During adoptive care, the adoptive parents already pay the child's upkeep. They can claim parental allowance (Elterngeld) and parental leave.
notes: Foster parents, by contrast, get no parental allowance.

rule_summary: Saarbrücken states the federal ages: one spouse must be at least 25 and the other at least 21.
Saxony sets 1,203 euro a month for ages 0 to 6 in 2026. That is 764 euro for material costs and 439 euro for care and upbringing.
notes: Ages 6 to 12: 1,362 euro. Ages 12 to 18: 1,511 euro. Notice of the Land youth office dated 22 October 2025. Saxony follows the Deutscher Verein by a 2022 decision.

rule_summary: Leipzig aims for an age gap of at most 45 years for a long-term placement. Older applicants can still apply.
notes: City practice in Leipzig.

rule_summary: Leipzig asks for enough space and a room of the child's own. Babies and toddlers do not need one at first.
notes: City practice in Leipzig. The room does not need to be ready during the check.

rule_summary: Leipzig foster parents must have no criminal record and no entries in the enhanced police certificate.
notes: City practice in Leipzig.

rule_summary: Leipzig's foster parent training runs on 3 Thursday evenings in a row at the adult education centre.
notes: City practice in Leipzig. Another part of the page calls it a 2-day course.

rule_summary: Leipzig foster parents must be able to cover their own living costs. The monthly payment covers the child's upkeep.
notes: City practice in Leipzig.

rule_summary: Leipzig foster parents need stable mental and physical health. Any illness must not limit daily life or parenting.
notes: City practice in Leipzig.

rule_summary: Since 2019 Saxony-Anhalt has set foster payments at the amounts the Deutscher Verein recommends, and made them legally binding.
notes: Social ministry press release of 4 February 2025. It says many other Länder do not make the amounts binding.

rule_summary: In Magdeburg, a first talk goes through forms and papers. Further one-to-one talks, a home visit and an applicant seminar follow.
notes: City practice.

rule_summary: Magdeburg asks for a questionnaire, a life story, an enhanced police certificate, proof of income and a doctor's certificate.
notes: From a search summary of the Magdeburg page. City practice.

rule_summary: Lübeck says the full application takes about 6 months, including courses, a home visit and closing talks.
notes: From a search summary; the page reset the connection. City practice.

rule_summary: Lübeck asks for the agreement of all family members, enough space, secure finances and an enhanced police certificate.
notes: From a search summary. City practice.

rule_summary: Thuringia's youth welfare act sets Land rules on granting, refusing and withdrawing a foster care permit.
legal_citation: ThürKJHAG § 21 (as cited by Altenburger Land district)
notes: We read the district's information sheet, not the act itself.

rule_summary: Altenburger Land asks for police certificates from every adult in the household, health certificates and a detailed life story.
notes: The sheet was written for people taking in children from Ukraine. District practice.

rule_summary: Altenburger Land makes at least 1 home visit to check living and hygiene conditions before granting a permit.
Jena's health office examines foster and adoption applicants for youth welfare offices. Per search results, adults pay 40 euro.
notes: The exam is free for children.

rule_summary: The Thuringia Land youth office sets the lump sums for full-time foster care.
notes: We did not find the 2026 amounts.
